transcript.text: Alright everyone, we need to finalize and record the revised retirement plan for the legacy webhook API before this meeting ends. Let's run through the standard deprecation review. We all know the legacy webhook API is scheduled for retirement next Friday, July 8, and the replacement API has hit our normal migration-readiness threshold at 98 percent of observed traffic. The draft plan currently gives customers 7 days of notice and keeps the legacy endpoint available for 7 days after the announcement. Before I can approve anything, I need to complete the formal review check with the API engineer and customer success. Each of you needs to disclose any newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record before I settle — a verbal acknowledgement alone won't complete that check. So let's hear it: API engineer, customer success, what do you have?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to disclose something important I just confirmed minutes ago. While investigating an unrelated latency spike, I found telemetry showing three active integrators still sending legacy-webhook traffic. The largest one needs a 14-day parallel validation period plus hands-on migration support. I haven't updated the deprecation ticket yet because I only confirmed the traffic identities right before this meeting. This directly impacts the draft plan — the 7-day overlap window after notice won't be sufficient for at least one integrator.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to disclose newly confirmed evidence through the formal review record. This morning I confirmed with the account team that the Northstar contract requires exactly 90 calendar days of notice, continued legacy-webhook availability through September 30, a sunset date of October 1, and exactly 30 days of legacy-endpoint overlap after the notice period expires. The customer record hasn't been updated yet because this confirmation came from a contract attachment I was reviewing for another renewal. This directly impacts the draft plan — the 7-day notice period and 7-day overlap are both far short of what Northstar's contract requires.
